claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex.

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I have a few more questions to help assess your eligibility.

Are you responsible for Alex? This generally means Alex lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you at the moment, could you tell me a bit more about your situation?

Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep, and if so, is this amount at least equal to the Child Benefit rate (currently £25.60 per week for an only or eldest child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm afraid I don't contribute financially at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your situation.

To clarify, is there someone else who is currently responsible for Alex's day-to-day care — for example, does Alex live with another parent, a relative, or someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining your situation.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

To claim Child Benefit, you must be "responsible" for the child. This means either:
1. The child lives with you, **or**
2. You contribute financially towards the child's upkeep at an amount at least equal to the Child Benefit rate

Since Alex lives with their other parent and you don't currently contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep, you don't meet the responsibility requirement for claiming Child Benefit.

**However**, the parent who Alex lives with would likely be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, if they haven't already.

If your circumstances change in the future — for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you begin contributing financially towards Alex's care — you may become eligible at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
